title: Redwood discovery - model selection (Marina Intel)
summary: Intro discovery call to understand Marina Intel's model selection needs: long context for compliance docs (~64k), multilingual coverage (EN/ES/FR/JP), tool-calling for database lookups and live pricing, and regulatory constraints requiring VPC/KMS. Discussed tradeoffs between Redwood Hosted, Dedicated and Private; recommended POC with two open models (LLaMA-3-32k variant and Mistral-8x-large) and a short benchmark for latency/cost/quality.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, jordan from Redwood here, i'm an AE. we got Priya from our SE team as well.
[00:12] Priya Raman: Hi all, hey, thanks for the time. quick agenda — understand your workload, context length, multilingual needs, tool-calling, and then we can propose candidate models and deployment modes.
[00:28] Carlos Mendes: Great, i'll do a quick background. I'm Carlos, Head of ML at Marina Intel. we do maritime logistics analytics, a lot of contracts and compliance text — long docs. we also support customers in LATAM and EMEA so spanish/french are big.
[00:43] Aisha Khan: hi, Aisha here, eng mgr. primary needs are generate summaries of contracts, answer questions over long docs (we're talking up to 60k tokens sometimes), and integrate with our pricing service via function calls. latency target is sub-second for short queries and <2s tail for doc search, and cost needs to be reasonable.
[01:05] Leo Park: and i'm leo, CTO. security is a hard requirement — SOC 2, SSO/SAML, KMS for keys, and we may need a private deployment or VPC option for certain customers.
[01:18] Jordan Lee: perfect — that's helpful. can you tell us what you're using now?
[01:22] Carlos Mendes: currently prototypes on OpenAI gpt-4o-ish stuff via public API for experiments, and some on-prem Llama 2 forks. latency and cost were variable; also the 32k context is hit-and-miss.
[01:35] Priya Raman: okay that maps. on models — from Redwood's side we support a bunch of open models and variants. for long-context we can offer 32k and 64k context variants. typical candidates are LLaMA-3 32k-style, Mistral long-context flavours, and some Luminous or other community models. note: names sometimes get fuzzy in transcripts — but we'll send a model matrix.
[01:58] Carlos Mendes: yeah, model quality vs cost — we need high factuality on contracts, hallucinations are a blocker. also multilingual — how good are these models in spanish/japanese?
[02:12] Priya Raman: short answer: LLaMA-3 style models tend to do well across languages, Mistral variants are strong on instruction and low-latency. For Japanese we recommend model finetune or in-context examples; we have evals showing relative strengths. quantization and 4-bit kernels can reduce cost but sometimes slightly affect quality — we can run your test prompts.
[02:37] Aisha Khan: tool calling — can we do function or tool calls? we need structured responses to hit our pricing API and we want guaranteed schema outputs.
[02:45] Jordan Lee: yes — Redwood hosted supports function/tool calling and structured outputs, streaming too. for Dedicated/Private you get the same runtime features; it's mostly about network and isolation. the SE can walk you through the function schema mapping.
[03:00] Priya Raman: important note — function calling throughput depends on batching and model latency. if you need sub-second cold-call latency for small queries, Dedicated with pinned instances is often best. Hosted can do it too but with heavier SLAs you'd look at Dedicated.
[03:20] Leo Park: on Private — do you support VPC peering or on-prem air-gapped installs? KMS integrations?
[03:26] Jordan Lee: yes, we have Redwood Private with VPC options and on-prem packages for regulated deployments; KMS/HSM support for keys, audit logs, and SAML/SSO integrations. we also provide SOC 2 artifacts.
[03:38] Carlos Mendes: ok tradeoffs — cost estimates?
[03:40] Priya Raman: high-level: open model variants quantized reduce token compute cost significantly. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower tail latency but requires reserved capacity (monthly commit). Hosted is consumption-based and fastest to set up. For Private there's a platform fee plus support. We'll send a cost model comparing token cost, pod cost, and predicted TCO for your volume.
[04:05] Aisha Khan: sample sizes — what's the recommended POC?
[04:08] Priya Raman: recommend two-model POC: one LLaMA-3-32k variant (higher quality/multilingual) and one Mistral-8x-long (fast/cost-efficient). run three tiers of tests: 1) quality on contract Q&A and summarization, 2) throughput/latency with your traffic profile, 3) function-calling schema reliability. we can run these in Hosted trial or spin a short Dedicated pilot.
[04:35] Carlos Mendes: duration?
[04:36] Jordan Lee: 2–3 weeks for initial eval with your representative dataset. Priya will help set up eval harness.
[04:42] Priya Raman: also will test quantized kernels (4-bit/8-bit) and measure hallucination rate; we'll log per-token latency and memory footprint.
[04:52] Aisha Khan: multilingual — will we need per-language finetunes?
[04:55] Priya Raman: likely not at first — prompt engineering + few-shot often enough for Spanish/French. For Japanese, if you need high fidelity we recommend a small finetune or retrieval-augmented prompts. we'll quantify in the POC.
[05:10] Leo Park: any competitors concerns? we evaluated Anthropic and Bedrock; what's your tilt vs them?
[05:15] Jordan Lee: Redwood focuses on production-first serving and flexible deployment modes — you get identical API and rollouts across Hosted, Dedicated, Private, plus observability/trace/rollout controls. we'll surface per-route cost/latency. competitors might offer model bundles but less emphasis on unified runtime and deployments.
[05:35] Carlos Mendes: good. last — data retention and logs for compliance?
[05:40] Jordan Lee: Hosted retains minimal logs and you can opt into reduced retention; Dedicated can isolate logs and Private leaves logs within your environment; full audit trails and SIEM integration available.
[05:50] Aisha Khan: ok thanks. next steps?
[05:52] Jordan Lee: recap: we'll send a model matrix + security whitepaper, pricing comparison, and propose a 2-model POC. Priya will own the benchmark setup. schedule follow-up next week to finalize the POC scope.
[06:05] Carlos Mendes: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[06:09] Jordan Lee: thanks, we'll follow up with the links and the deck.
